title: First Night
notes: Welcome to Exit 13. You're the new night auditor. Your shift runs 10 PM to 6 AM. Previous auditor quit without notice. Read the binder on the counter for procedures. Key duties: ring up customers, authorize fuel pumps, check in motel guests, keep the place clean. Don't overthink anything. It's a gas station. Clock in and do the work.

title: Settling In
notes: Supply delivery tonight between midnight and 2 AM. Guest in Room 3 complained about noise from an empty room. Radio has been acting up - ignore it. Don't forget to restock the cooler. Revenue was low last week, let's improve that.

title: The Request
notes: Storm advisory for Highway 13 corridor, expected after midnight. Someone called asking about Room 4. Room 4 has been closed for years. Do not open it. Do not discuss it with guests. The radio should be off. If it's on, turn it off. Storm prep: check all exterior lights, close storm shutters if available.

title: The Deputy
notes: Highway power outage reported between Mile 80 and Mile 95. Deputy Hale may stop by to check the property. Be cooperative but brief. DO NOT go into the basement. The access is sealed for structural reasons. Focus on the job. Keep the lights on.

title: Locked Doors
notes: New locks have been installed. Don't ask why. Incident log is available in the office if you want to review it. Motel occupancy has been strange this week. Some check-ins don't match the ledger. Not your problem. Do the job. Note: the freezer compressor has been running loud. Call maintenance if it gets worse.

title: The Frequency
notes: County ranger will do a perimeter check tonight. Highway reported several vehicles stalled near Mile 87, tow services dispatched. The radio is NOT an emergency frequency. Do not respond to it. I repeat: do not respond to anything on the radio. It is not real. Focus on customers and keep the till accurate.

title: The Warning
notes: Stop asking questions. I know you've been looking at old records. The archive is not for staff. The radio is interference, nothing more. Room 4 stays sealed. The basement stays locked. Mile 87 is just a stretch of highway. People have accidents. It's not your concern. Do the job I'm paying you for or don't come back. This is your only warning.

title: Mile 87
notes: The owner's lying. The radio is real. I've heard the dispatch calls - they match the accident from three years ago. The pileup at Mile 87 killed eleven people and they never recovered all the vehicles. Some of those people have been checking into this motel. I have the old invoices. I have the dispatch transcripts. Tonight I find out what's in the basement.

title: The Loop
notes: Exit 13 isn't a place. It's a waystation. The highway remembers what happened. The people who died at Mile 87 keep arriving because someone keeps accepting them. The motel logs go back decades - same guests, same rooms, same nights. You've been processing the dead, Mara. And someone has been profiting from it. The owner knows. The deputy knows. The question is: do you keep the station open, or do you shut it down?

title: Last Shift
notes: This is it. Everything converges tonight. The highway, the guests, the storm, the radio, Room 4, the basement, the owner, the deputy - all of it comes to a head. Your choices across every shift determine what happens. There are four ways this ends. Clock in one last time.
